what_it_does_now: BOTH instances must be claimed with a complete, confirmed identity before ANY shared step: the demonstration reads and writes across A and B, so one side belonging to somebody else is a reason to stop rather than to carry on with the other
if either is refused or incomplete, it runs no shared step and only bounded cleanup for what it legitimately claimed

every write and every stop -- normal path and cleanup alike -- goes through ONE gate that refuses an instance this run does not own, so a later edit cannot walk around the filter the way the normal path just did
the run reports which instances it touched, and touching an unclaimed one is a failure rather than a line in a log

what_the_controls_establish.the_positive_controls_still_work: selector-changed still fails on the preservation assertion, stop-nonzero and cleanup-raises still report unresolved cleanup, and every one of them shows unclaimed_touched empty

what_was_wrong: ownership was established per instance and then asked as `if not owned:` -- 'did I claim ANYTHING?'. With A fresh and B already running, A was claimed, B was refused, and the shared lifecycle ran anyway: it corrupted B's selector and called the normal-path stop(B) on an instance this run did not own. In the reverse order it stopped an unclaimed A. The cleanup filter was right; the normal path walked around it.
